doc_friction.issue: Searched open PRs only after building and timing (about 40 min in); PR #16028 had been open as a draft for the same item since 00:11. Searching before starting a Critique target, not only before opening the PR, would have caught it. The doc's 'before opening a PR' timing is what I followed, and it was too late.

Critique mode sends every process run to the same measure 'doc friction' table, so two runs started in the same hour picked the same top ungated item (perf suite timings). A claim step (open the draft PR first, as #16028 did) is the only guard; the prompt says 'check open PRs before you start' but the measure output gives no hint which items are already taken.

deviations.why: Dropped my own version of the tool (--table/--record) after finding PR #16028 shipped the same thing, rather than consolidating two implementations.
deviations.did: Waited for #16028 to merge, rebuilt the branch on main, and kept only the findings it lacked (second independent timing, scheduling lower bound).
deviations.result: Small follow-up PR, no duplicate code on main.

notes: Backlog had only owner rows; main_health 214/214 green. Critique target: doc friction 2026-11-14 (perf prompt 'no per-suite timing table'). Full run here: run_venture_tests.py --slowest 2000, 1,365 suites, 0 failed, 15m18s wall, 3,639 suite-s. Built --table/--record, then found duplicate PR #16028 (same tool, merged 00:5x). Follow-up keeps: second-reading comparison (top ten identical, top six same order; 37 suites >=5 s ratio 0.71-1.14, median 0.93) and the 910 s work bound vs 918 s run, which shows bytes-vs-seconds scheduling order cannot help. Checks: test_run_venture_tests 41/41, check_post_frontmatter ok, post_similarity 0 pairs, doc_index ok. Outcome partial: most of the session's work was duplicated.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a full timing run plus a short analysis and post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
